aspects.fertilizer:
**Ridge Planting:**
For ridge planting of Camelina (Sonai), broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation, run a plough and planker, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger-cum-seeder planter introduced by various companies is available in the market for this planting method.

**General Soil Fertility:**
Balanced and proportional fertilizer application protects Camelina (Sonai) from adverse climate change effects and improves yield.
Base per-acre fertilizer quantities on laboratory soil analysis.
For average fertility soils, apply fertilizers at the recommended rates.
For seed purchased from private companies, apply fertilizers according to the company recommendations.

**Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:**
Apply the entire quantity of fertilizer for Camelina (Sonai) at sowing time.

**Irrigated Areas:**
Apply the full amount of phosphorus and potash fertilizers along with one-third of the nitrogen fertilizer at sowing time.
Apply the remaining nitrogen fertilizer in two splits, giving half with the first irrigation and the other half before flowering.

**Sonai Naheel Crop:**
Sonai Naheel requires approximately three irrigations.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after sowing.
Apply the second irrigation at flowering.
Apply the third irrigation immediately after flowering ends.
Apply one bag of DAP and half a bag of SOP per acre at sowing time for better growth.
Apply one bag of ammonium sulfate per acre with the second irrigation.
Apply one bag of ammonium sulfate per acre with the third irrigation.

**Nutrient Substitutions and Supplements:**
Apply 4 to 5 kg of sulfur per acre with the second irrigation to improve yield and quality.
Use ammonium sulfate fertilizer instead of urea if it is available.
Boron application is beneficial for increased flowering and pollination.
If SOP is not available, MOP can be used, but 2 kg of sulfur per acre must be added with it.

**Punjab Fertilizer App and Testing:**
Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore developed a free mobile app named Khad Hisab available on the Google Play Store.
The Khad Hisab app calculates balanced fertilizer needs for Camelina (Sonai) and other crops to raise yields and profits, whether a soil test report is available or not.
Watch the short video in the app introduction box to learn how to use it.
Contact the nearest government soil and water testing laboratory for more information.
aspects.harvesting:
Harvesting Sonai Naheel:
Sonai Naheel matures in 120 to 150 days.
Harvest the crop when its leaves shed and it turns golden.
The yield potential of Sonai Naheel is 20 to 25 maunds per acre.

Seed Storage:
Ensure seeds are thoroughly dry before storage.
Moisture content in the seed must not exceed 8 percent.
A properly dry grain makes a cracking sound when chewed with teeth.
High moisture creates a risk of fungal attack.
Do not mix different varieties during storage.

Storage Pest Control:
Inspect warehouses regularly to protect stored Camelina from insect attacks.
Fumigate the store using 30 to 35 tablets of aluminum phosphide per 1000 cubic feet.

Spray Application and Waste Disposal:
Use a flat fan or floodjet nozzle for weed control.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insects.
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.

Domestic Oil Refining:
Domestic refining makes Camelina oil relatively cheap, pure, and nutritious for use as cooking oil.
First extract the oil using an expeller or kohlu.
Place 5 kilograms of crude Camelina oil in a pot or pan and heat it to 85 degrees Celsius.
Do not let the oil boil, but heat it enough that the pot cannot be touched by hand.
Add 150 grams of finely ground fuller's earth or gachni to the hot oil.
Stir well with a spoon for 5 minutes and remove it from the stove.
Make a triangular bag from thick market cloth.
Hang the bag from a sturdy stand or charpai and place a clean container underneath.
Pour the lukewarm oil into this bag to filter it.

Farmer Guidance:
The Directorate General of Agricultural Information runs an awareness campaign through print, electronic, and social media to provide timely guidance from sowing to harvesting.
aspects.irrigation:
**Irrigation Schedule:**
Camelina Sonai or Sonai Naheel requires approximately three irrigations.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after sowing.
Apply the second irrigation at the time of flowering.
Apply the third irrigation immediately after flowering ends.
Take special care of irrigation in case of drought.
Check the weather forecast before irrigating.

**Fertilizer Application:**
Apply one bag of DAP and half a bag of SOP per acre at sowing time.
Apply one bag of Ammonium Sulphate per acre with the second irrigation.
Apply one bag of Ammonium Sulphate per acre with the third irrigation.

**Termite Control:**
To prevent expected termite attack, apply recommended poison in the empty field during soaking irrigation.
If a termite attack occurs on the crop, flood the recommended poison with irrigation water.

**Rain-fed Barani Areas:**
In barani areas, mix recommended poison with 15 to 20 kilograms of fine soil.
Broadcast this mixture in the field before sowing and plow the land.

**Field and Weather Management:**
To protect against excessive rainfall, sow Camelina Sonai on ridges to minimize crop damage and make excess water drainage easy.
Sow the crop at the recommended time for better care.
Take special care of plant protection.
Stay informed about the weather forecast before sowing.
aspects.machinery:
Ridge planting:
Camelina is also called Sonai.
Broadcast seed and fertilizer after preparing the land.
Run a plow and planking.
Make ridges at a distance of 2.5 feet using a tractor.
Different companies have introduced a planter called a ridger-cum-seeder for this planting method.
The ridger-cum-seeder is available in the market.

Spraying calibration and precautions:
Before spraying the Camelina crop, fill the machine with plain water to check it and determine the water quantity.
Use the recommended water quantity to ensure uniform spray coverage.
Do not stand against the direction of the wind during spraying.
Do not spray during strong winds.
Avoid using poisons from the same chemical group repeatedly.

Nozzle selection:
Use a flat fan nozzle or a flood jet nozzle for weed control in Camelina.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect control.

Pesticide waste disposal:
Bury empty poison bottles in the ground.
Dispose of cardboard boxes.
aspects.other:
Harvesting greens:
Farmers commonly pluck greens from the Camelina (Sonai) crop.
Plucking greens increases the risk of aphid attack on the crop.
Plucking greens reduces crop yield.
Allocate a separate area for obtaining greens within a crop sown for seed to protect the remaining crop from damage.

Climate change management:
Climate change harms Camelina (Sonai) through unexpected rains, excessive rains, or drought.
Sow the crop at the recommended time to protect it from the effects of climate change.
Ensure plant protection.
Stay informed about the weather forecast before sowing or irrigating.

High rainfall areas:
Mandatorily sow Camelina on ridges in high rainfall areas.
aspects.overview:
Punjab Statistics:
In 2020-21, Camelina Sonai area was 413.50 thousand acres or 167.34 thousand hectares, total production was 267.26 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 16.16 maunds per acre.
In 2021-22, area was 585.50 thousand acres or 236.94 thousand hectares, total production was 403.00 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 17.21 maunds per acre.
In 2022-23, area was 1055.10 thousand acres or 426.98 thousand hectares, total production was 665.71 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.77 maunds per acre.
In 2023-24, area was 605.20 thousand acres or 244.91 thousand hectares, total production was 314.47 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 12.99 maunds per acre.
According to 2024-25 provisional estimates, area was 820.65 thousand acres or 332.10 thousand hectares, total production was 499.94 thousand metric tons, and average yield was 15.23 maunds per acre.

Crop Characteristics:
Camelina Sonai seed contains 35 to 37 percent high quality oil.
The oil has low saturated fatty acids and over 20 percent omega-3 which helps lower cholesterol.
The crop naturally possesses extremely high resistance to diseases, pests, and shattering.
Production potential is 20 to 25 maunds per acre.

Variety and Seed Sources:
The Oilseeds Department at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad approved the variety named Sonai Naheel.
Sonai Naheel has improved resistance against climate change.
Seed is available from the Oilseeds Department at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad and select private companies.

Soil and Land Preparation:
Camelina Sonai can be cultivated on all soil types.
Do not cultivate in highly saline or waterlogged soils.
Prepare the land thoroughly and level it with a laser land leveler.

Sowing and Harvesting:
The suitable sowing time for Sonai Naheel is October 10 to November 10.
It can also be sown from early September to the end of November.
The crop matures in 120 to 150 days.
Harvest the crop when its leaves shed and it turns golden.

Agricultural Extension and Promotion:
The 2025-26 oilseed production plan includes canola, mustard, raya, taramira, linseed, and camelina to reduce edible oil imports.
Promotion begins with publishing the production plan.
Extension staff writes recommendations and slogans on walls, boundary pillars, and signboards.
Deputy Directors of Agriculture Extension formulate integrated district strategies and report to the provincial government.
Progressive farmers are introduced to newly developed varieties.
Agricultural experts conduct training programs at district and tehsil levels for extension staff and farmers.
The Directorate General of Agricultural Information runs awareness campaigns through print, electronic, and social media from sowing to harvest.
aspects.pests_diseases:
General Resistance:
Camelina resists diseases, insect pests, and shattering.

Seed Treatment:
Treat seed with recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kilogram seed.
Maintain accurate water and chemical levels to avoid harming germination.
Avoid early sowing to control wilt.

Grain Storage:
Fumigate warehouses using 30 to 35 aluminum phosphide tablets per 1000 cubic feet.

Termite Management:
Apply recommended chemical during rauni in empty fields.
Flood 1 liter Fipronil 5 percent SC per acre with irrigation water.

Barani Termite Management:
Mix recommended poison with 15 to 20 kilograms fine soil, broadcast before sowing, and plow.

Surface Grasshopper Management:
Spray 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC per acre.
Attack risk is higher near sugarcane, maize, and sorghum.

Mustard Sawfly Management:
Larvae attack in October and November.
Spray per acre 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 330 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 percent EC, 200 milliliters Emamectin benzoate 1.9 EC, or 30 grams Fipronil 80 WG.

Painted Bug Management:
Insects measure 5 to 7 millimeters and attack during October and November.
Spray per acre 400 milliliters Abamectin plus Thiamethoxam 108 SC, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 250 grams Acephate 75 SP, or 250 milliliters Bifenthrin 10 EC.

Cabbage Butterfly Management:
Spray per acre 80 milliliters Chlorantraniliprole plus Thiamethoxam 300 SC, 80 milliliters Spinetoram 120 SC, 50 milliliters Flubendiamide 480 SC, or 250 milliliters Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC.

Aphid Management:
Complete sowing during the first week of October.
Aphids attack in clusters from mid-January to late March.
Spray per acre 24 grams Thiamethoxam 25 SWG, 100 grams Dinotefuran 20 percent SG, 60 grams Flonicamid 50 WG, or 200 milliliters Clothianidin 20 EC.

Punjab Biological Control:
Release Chrysoperla green lacewing cards against aphids.
Punjab Agriculture Extension provides cards free from eleven laboratories in Sahiwal, Faisalabad, Hafizabad, Layyah, Vehari, Pakpattan, Sheikhupura, Jhang, Muzaffargarh, Okara, and Toba Tek Singh.

Disease Management:
For white rust, spray 1.25 milliliters Propiconazole or Difenoconazole per liter water.
For Alternaria blight during rain at 10 to 25 degrees Celsius, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole per liter water.
For downy mildew, spray 5 grams Flumorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium or 6 grams Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil per liter water.
For bacterial stem rot during smog, spray 2.5 milliliters Benzothiazolinone, 1 gram Streptomycin sulfate, or 6 milliliters Kasugamycin per liter water.
For Sclerotinia stem rot, treat seed with 1 gram Thiophanate-methyl per kilogram seed, or spray 2.5 milliliters Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole per liter water.
For seedling blight, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 3.5 grams Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin per liter water.
For camelina rust, spray 1 gram Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin or 2 milliliters Propiconazole per liter water.

Safety and Spray Rules:
Spray at economic thresholds during evening.
Use hollow cone nozzles for insects and flat fan or flood jet nozzles for weeds.
Do not hoe immediately after spraying.
aspects.sowing:
Variety and Seed:
Camelina Sonai or Sonai Naheel resists diseases, pests, and shattering.
Seed is available from the Oilseeds Department at Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad and private companies.

Sowing Time:
The recommended sowing period is October 10 to November 10.
Sowing can also occur from early September to late November.

Land Preparation:
Camelina Sonai grows on all soil types except highly saline and waterlogged soils.
Prepare land thoroughly and level using a laser land leveler.
Ensure seed depth does not exceed 1.5 inches.

Sowing Methods and Rates:
Sowing is done by drill, gapp chhat, and on ridges.
For drill sowing, maintain 12 to 18 inches between rows, 4 to 5 inches between plants, and use 1 to 1.5 kg seed per acre.
For ridge sowing via dibbling, use 500 grams seed per acre.
For ridge cultivation, broadcast seed and fertilizer after land preparation, run a plough and planker, and make ridges 2.5 feet apart using a tractor.
A ridger-cum-seeder planter is commercially available.
Ridge sowing minimizes damage from heavy rainfall and eases excess water drainage.

Fertilizer:
Apply 1 bag of DAP and half bag of SOP per acre at sowing.

Weed Control:
For drill and wattar sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray S-metolachlor at 800 ml per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
When temperatures are 35 degrees Celsius or below, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.

Thinning:
Complete thinning before the first irrigation.
Thin when plants develop 4 leaves, removing weak and diseased plants.
Maintain 9 to 12 inches spacing between healthy plants.

Irrigation:
The crop requires approximately 3 irrigations.
Apply the first irrigation 25 to 30 days after sowing.
Apply the second irrigation at flowering.
Apply the third irrigation immediately after flowering ends.
Manage irrigation carefully during drought.

Pest Management:
To prevent termites, apply recommended chemical during pre-sowing irrigation in empty fields.
If termites attack, flood the chemical with irrigation water.

Rain-fed (Barani) Areas:
Conserving summer monsoon moisture increases Rabi crop yields by 20 to 25 percent.
Before monsoon, deep plough empty fields, strengthen bunds, level land, and plough across slopes.
Do not plough after the monsoon season.
Before sowing, plough twice and plank to retain moisture.
Prepare land in the evening or before sunrise.
At sowing, fields must be level and weed-free.
For termites, mix recommended poison into 15 to 20 kg fine soil, broadcast before sowing, and plough.

General Advisory:
Sow at recommended times, prioritize plant protection, and check weather forecasts before sowing or irrigating.
aspects.varieties:
Seed Sources:
Limited seed is available from Punjab Seed Corporation, National Agricultural Research Centre Islamabad, Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad, Camelina Research Centre Khanpur, Regional Agricultural Research Institute Bahawalpur, and Barani Agricultural Research Institute Chakwal. Recommended varieties are also available from registered private seed companies. Farmers should always use seed certified by the Federal Seed Certification Department.

Varieties and Characteristics:
Camelina Sonai is a new oilseed crop naturally resistant to diseases, pests, and shattering. It contains 35 to 37 percent high quality oil with low saturated fatty acids and over 20 percent Omega-3. Ayub Agricultural Research Institute Faisalabad approved the variety Sonai Naheel, which has improved climate resilience. 

Sowing Dates:
The optimal sowing time for Sonai Naheel is October 10 to November 10. Sowing can also occur from early September to late November.

Soil and Land Preparation:
Camelina can be grown on all soil types, but not on highly saline or waterlogged soils. Prepare the field thoroughly and level it using a laser land leveler. Sowing depth must not exceed 1.5 inches.

Sowing Methods and Seed Rates:
Crops can be sown by drill, broadcast in wet soil, or on ridges. For drill sowing, keep row spacing at 12 to 18 inches and plant spacing at 4 to 5 inches. The general seed rate is 1 to 1.5 kg per acre. For ridge sowing using the dibbling method, 500 grams of seed per acre is sufficient.

Seed Treatment:
Apply recommended fungicide at 1 gram per kg of seed. Do not exceed chemical doses and use appropriate water to avoid harming germination. Do not apply fungicide if accurate dosing cannot be maintained.

Epidemic Blight:
Prevent by using healthy seed, rotating crops, and destroying residues. When temperatures are 10 to 25 degrees Celsius during rainy conditions, apply a preventive spray of Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

Plant Blight:
Sow resistant varieties, rotate crops, and treat seeds with recommended fungicide. When symptoms appear, spray Tebuconazole plus Trifloxystrobin at 1 gram per liter of water, or Metiram plus Pyraclostrobin at 3.5 grams per liter of water.

Downy Mildew:
Use healthy seed and destroy crop residues. When symptoms appear, spray Fluomorph plus Fosetyl-aluminium at 5 grams per liter of water, or Mancozeb plus Cymoxanil at 6 grams per liter of water.

Stem Rot:
Treat seed at sowing with Thiophanate-methyl at 1 gram per kg of seed. If symptoms appear on the crop, spray Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2.5 ml per liter of water.

Wilt:
Wilt causes seed rot, drying of plants, and cracked root bark. Control by sowing fungicide-treated seed, avoiding early sowing, eradicating weeds, and practicing crop rotation.
aspects.weeds:
**Common weeds:**
Common weeds in Camelina include wild oat, dumbi sitti, lashkani booti, bathu, karund, shahtra, and itsit.

**Non-chemical weed control:**
The daab method is suitable for weed destruction.
After soaking irrigation or rain, when the soil reaches wattar moisture condition, plough and apply a heavy planker.
Leave the field for 5 to 7 days so weeds germinate and get destroyed during final seedbed preparation.
Perform dry hoeing after crop emergence, preferably before rain, to destroy existing weeds.
Do the first hoeing before the first irrigation.
Do the second hoeing after irrigation when the soil returns to wattar moisture condition.
Thin the crop when it develops four leaves to maintain the recommended plant spacing.
Strictly avoid hoeing immediately after herbicide application.
Hoeing right after spraying breaks the chemical barrier, allows weeds to re-emerge, and raises dust carrying chemicals that harm farmer health through skin contact and breathing.

**Chemical weed control:**
If heavy weed infestation is expected, apply recommended herbicides immediately after sowing.
In moderate weather when the temperature is 35 degrees Celsius or lower, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor mixed in 100 liters of water per acre immediately after sowing.
For drill and wattar sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre before the final ploughing.
For ridge sowing, spray 800 ml S-metolachlor per acre within 24 hours after sowing.
For pre-emergence control, spray 1000 ml Pendimethalin per acre.
To eliminate itsit that emerges within two weeks of crop emergence, spray 400 to 500 ml Metazachlor 50 percent SC per acre.
Metazachlor spray can be applied without using a protective shield.

**Spraying equipment and disposal:**
Use a flat fan or flood jet nozzle for weed control sprays.
Use a hollow cone nozzle for insect pest sprays.
Bury empty pesticide bottles in the soil and destroy cardboard boxes.

**Wilt and root rot control:**
In wilt or root rot, seeds rot, plants dry up, and root bark appears cracked.
To manage wilt, destroy weeds, treat seed with recommended fungicides, avoid early sowing, and rotate crops.
